title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Final Surcharge Amount and Rounding to the Cent
content:
## Clause

The amount of the Dangerous Goods Acceptance hazardous-cargo surcharge is the surcharge per container after discount multiplied by the number of containers on the acceptance. That product is the only figure ever rounded: it is expressed exactly in cents and brought to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being raised to the cent above. The per-container figures on the way to it are held in hundredths and ten-thousandths of a dollar precisely so that none of them is rounded.

The amount to book is 0.00 in three situations: the acceptance is light enough to be surcharge-free, the acceptance already carries its hazardous-cargo surcharge entry, or the goods have not reached the point at which the surcharge falls due. In every other situation it is the rounded product.

## Worked examples (invented figures)

| Per container after discount | Containers | Exact product | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| 409.20 | 3 | 1227.60 | 1227.60 |
| 219.9375 | 2 | 439.875 | 439.88 |
| 110.055 | 1 | 110.055 | 110.06 |
| 219.9375 | 4 | 879.75 | 879.75 |

## Point of judgement

**What becomes of an exact half cent?** It goes up to the next whole cent, as the third example shows.
